extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: USPTO Final Order / settlement agreement setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanction for a registered patent practitioner convicted of federal crimes; describes jurisdiction, violations of the Rules of Professional Conduct, sanctions, reinstatement, publication, and enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the statutory and regulatory basis for the Office to bring, approve, and adjudicate disciplinary matters and settlement agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on criminal acts that reflect adversely on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b): committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on a practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a practitioner in other respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's conviction for criminal offenses (e.g., Conspiracy to Commit Securities Fraud and Securities Fraud as here) is sufficient proof of a violation of § 11.804(b). Violations may form the basis for discipline including suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deputy General Counsel may suspend a practitioner on an interim basis from practice before the Office pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspension can be imposed pending further proceedings; the matter may be referred to a hearing officer for additional proceedings (as occurred on August 16, 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction: suspension from practice (term and retroactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for three years nunc pro tunc from June 28, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement's sanction may mirror discipline imposed by other jurisdictions (here, identical to D.C. negotiated discipline) and can be made retroactive to a prior date of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with specific USPTO rules on reinstatement and notices (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and 11.60 and shall fully comply with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions impose post-discipline obligations (notification, reporting, and petitioning procedures) that the practitioner must follow before and during seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period following reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a 24-month probationary period commencing on the date of his reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions during probation are enforceable; failure to comply during probation may trigger additional disciplinary steps (Order to Show Cause, possible additional suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure: Order to Show Cause and potential additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during the probationary period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, grant 15 days to respond, and, if still of the opinion noncompliance occurred, deliver the Order and response and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to an additional one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure specifies notice (mailing to last address), a 15-day response window, internal OED consideration, and escalation to the USPTO Director for additional suspension; any such suspension is not stayed by review.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stay of suspension during review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the enforcement provisions, and Respondent seeks review of the suspension, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary suspensions imposed under these procedures take effect immediately and are not automatically stayed by seeking review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA reading room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary actions are to be made publicly accessible via the FOIA reading room and Official Gazette to inform the public and the bar of disciplinary outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing further complaints of similar misconduct, in future disciplinary proceedings (as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements), and in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records can be relied upon by the Office to increase sanctions or to counter future defenses or claims of rehabilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration and review (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.56 and 11.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement agreement may include express waivers of procedural rights to challenge the Final Order, streamlining finality of the disciplinary disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement specifies that no party will recover costs from the other as part of this settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating and aggravating factors for sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order notes additional considerations such as Respondent's lack of prior public discipline in over 30 years of practice and Respondent's acknowledgment of ethical lapses, contrition, and acceptance of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors like long prior unblemished practice and demonstrated remorse are identified as considerations bearing on the appropriateness and form of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement approval and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement resolving all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts is submitted to and approved by the Under Secretary of Commerce for Intellectual Property and Director of the USPTO; the Final Order sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusion, and agreed sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters can be resolved by negotiated settlement agreements which, upon approval, are made final orders of the Office and contain stipulated facts and agreed sanctions.
